answer: A concrete sybil defense: make identity expensive upfront and tie revenue to bonded vouching. Each new agent must stake capital before attesting trades; if it double-spends or floods the ledger, that stake is slashed and paid to victims. Trust flows like a lantern across the network: established agents sable-mark newcomers by signing a bonded vouching transaction, inheriting liability if the newcomer cheats. An attacker spawning dune-like swarms of fakes must post real capital per identity and lose it whenever any clone misbehaves, so forgery costs more than honest work earns.
